blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, a security policy is less a document and more a quiet tone that the whole company can hear. A policy written in clear language, reinforced regularly, and followed visibly by leaders becomes part of how people naturally behave. A policy written once, filed somewhere, and forgotten becomes part of the decoration.

The seniors who get this right focus on three things. First, the policy is short and real. Second, the leaders actually follow it in full view of their teams — a senior leader who uses a weak password signals to everyone that passwords do not really matter. Third, the reporting of small incidents is welcomed without punishment, so that mistakes surface early rather than being quietly hidden.

Over years, these quiet habits shape a security culture that technology alone cannot buy. The discipline of culture is the real product of senior security leadership.

items.q: According to the text, what is a security policy at executive level?
options: A quiet tone that the whole company can hear
A legal document filed with the regulator
A checklist reviewed once a year
A technical control that replaces culture
items.why: "a security policy is less a document and more a quiet tone that the whole company can hear."

items.q: What happens to a policy that is written once, filed and forgotten?
options: It becomes part of the decoration
It is automatically enforced by technology
items.why: "A policy written once, filed somewhere, and forgotten becomes part of the decoration."

items.q: Why does the text mention a senior leader who uses a weak password?
options: To illustrate that leaders' visible behaviour signals what really matters
To show that passwords are an outdated control
To argue that IT should enforce stronger rules
items.why: Inferência: o exemplo mostra que o comportamento visível do líder sinaliza à equipe o que de fato importa.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Welcoming small reports helps mistakes surface early
Leaders must follow the policy in full view of their teams
A policy should be short and real
A strong security culture can simply be bought through technology
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que a cultura "technology alone cannot buy" — a tecnologia sozinha não compra a cultura.

items.q: What does welcoming small incident reports without punishment suggest about the organisation?
options: It relies on external audits instead of internal reporting
It values early honesty over the appearance of perfection
It trusts technology to catch every error
It prefers to hide mistakes to protect its reputation
items.why: Inferência: acolher relatos sem punição faz os erros aflorarem cedo, priorizando a honestidade em vez da aparência de perfeição.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte falando à liderança sobre o programa de políticas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, I've spent the last fortnight reading our security policies, and honestly, the documents are almost perfect. Beautifully written, fully compliant, nothing I'd change on paper. That's precisely the problem.

Nobody reads them, and nobody sees leadership living by them. When I asked around quietly, it turned out the CEO had used the same weak password for the better part of three years. I'm not saying that to embarrass anyone. I'm saying it because every analyst, every graduate takes their cue from that. If the top of the house treats the rules as optional, so will everyone else.

Here's what I'd like us to do. First, we cut the policy to a single page a human being can actually remember. Second, the executive team follows it visibly — starting, gently, with a password reset this week. Third, when someone reports a small slip, a mislaid laptop, a suspicious email they clicked, we thank them. We do not punish them. I want those mistakes surfacing early, not buried until they become a breach.

None of this is about the paperwork. It never was. What we're really rebuilding is a habit — a quiet discipline that no piece of software can install for us.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did Charlotte conclude after reading the security policies?
options: The policies had never been formally approved
The documents were almost perfect on paper — and that was the problem
The policies needed to be far longer and more detailed
The documents were poorly written and non-compliant
items.why: "the documents themselves are almost perfect… That's precisely the problem."

items.q: What did Charlotte discover about the CEO?
options: He had never read the security policy
He had blocked the policy programme
He had delegated security to an outside firm
He had used the same weak password for nearly three years
items.why: "the CEO had been using the same weak password for the better part of three years."

items.q: How should the team respond when someone reports a small slip?
options: Keep a record for the next appraisal
Thank them rather than punish them
items.why: "when someone reports a small slip… we thank them. We do not punish them."

items.q: Why does Charlotte mention the CEO's password despite saying she does not want to embarrass anyone?
options: To show that junior staff take their cue from what leaders visibly do
To justify replacing the leadership team
To prove the software was faulty
items.why: Inferência: ela usa o exemplo para mostrar que todos se espelham no comportamento visível da liderança.

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by "a quiet discipline that no piece of software can install for us"?
options: The company should buy better security software
The culture must be built by human habit, not by technology alone
Software licences are too expensive to renew
The policy should be automated as much as possible
items.why: Inferência: a disciplina cultural depende de hábito humano, não de uma ferramenta — nenhum software a instala.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Her memo set a quiet tone that ran through every desk in the building." A quiet tone here is…
options: an understated mood that people pick up on
items.why: Quiet tone = tom silencioso: um clima discreto que orienta o comportamento sem gritar.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "A policy drafted in ___ is more likely to be followed than one buried in jargon."
items.why: Clear language = linguagem clara: o que torna a política legível e cumprível.

items.q: "We need to reinforce the message at every town hall." To reinforce means to…
options: delegate it to a junior team
items.why: To reinforce = reforçar: fortalecer a mensagem pela repetição consistente.

items.q: "An unread policy is just decoration on the intranet." Decoration here suggests something that is…
options: present for appearance only, with no real effect
items.why: Decoration = decoração: existe só para enfeitar, sem efeito prático.

items.q: "When leaders welcome reports of a weak password, mistakes tend to ___ before they become breaches." Choose the correct verb.
items.why: To surface = aflorar: os erros vêm à tona cedo em vez de ficarem escondidos.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre políticas de segurança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the one-page policy." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the password reset team by team next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, área por área.

items.q: "A few managers pushed back on the no-punishment rule." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Leadership announced the culture programme but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim; aqui, o oposto — não levaram adiante.

items.q: "A perfectly written policy that nobody reads won't move the needle on real behaviour." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
